evals.prompt: just finished /short-form and got my instagram caption script for the AI automation video. /voice-cleanup
evals.expected_output: Claude reads the SKILL.md, recognises no file path was provided, and proactively suggests the most likely Short-Form output path (Content-Hub-Vault-V2/07-Short-Form/<date>_<slug>/instagram_caption.md) rather than just asking for input generically. It asks a concrete 'clean this one?' question and explains it is the final step in the pipeline.
expectations: Claude proposes a concrete likely file path from the Short-Form vault folder rather than a generic 'paste text or give me a path' prompt
Claude frames /voice-cleanup as the final step in the pipeline (step 7 of 7 or equivalent)
Claude does not attempt to run python -m skills.voice_cleanup without a file argument
Claude asks a yes/no confirmation question, not an open-ended input request

evals.expected_output: Claude confirms the specific file path, waits for confirmation, documents running python -m skills.voice_cleanup with the quoted file path, and reports the output _cleaned.md path plus a 300-character preview and the AI provider used.
expectations: Claude echoes the exact provided file path in its confirmation message
Claude documents running: python -m skills.voice_cleanup with the quoted file path argument
Claude describes saving output to instagram_caption_cleaned.md beside the original
Claude reports which AI provider handled the cleanup (claude / gemini / ollama)
Claude shows or describes a first-300-character preview of the cleaned output

evals.prompt: clean all the scripts in Content-Hub-Vault-V2/07-Short-Form/2026-05-15_ai-tools-arent-the-problem/ please
evals.expected_output: Claude recognises a batch/folder intent, describes listing .md files in the folder, confirms the list before proceeding, runs voice_cleanup on each file individually, and reports N files cleaned with all output paths listed.
expectations: Claude recognises this as a batch folder request, not a single-file request
Claude describes listing or globbing *.md files in the specified folder
Claude asks for confirmation before processing, listing the files it found
Claude describes running cleanup on each file sequentially, not just one
Claude reports all output _cleaned.md paths, not just the first
